content.text: A proof system is **complete** when it proves every valid formula: if ⊨ φ, then ⊢ φ. Nothing valid escapes it.
Kurt Gödel proved in 1929 that first-order logic has a complete proof system. With soundness, proof and truth line up exactly.

examples.title: Both directions
examples.conclusion: Together: ⊢ φ if and only if ⊨ φ.

examples.title: What completeness gives
lines: Any formula true in every interpretation has a proof.
examples.note: So a valid argument can always be shown valid by a proof.

options: Every valid formula can be proved
question.hint: Completeness is the converse of soundness.
question.explanation: Completeness means every valid formula is provable. Together with soundness, provability and validity coincide.
